title: Larry with an AR-15 aboard a helicopter
description: Larry, wind-tossed and intent, sits inside a helicopter gripping an AR-15 upright beside him — the first time he had ever seen one, he says. The rifle belonged to someone else on the helicopter; he held it and put on an expression for the camera. His assumption is they were heading back to headquarters.
researchNotes: Relayed by Larry's son from Larry's dictation (2026-08-15 session; archived as data/recollections/giscus-vn-0029-c18035474.json and -c18035478.json). Period detail rings true: in 1964–65 the AR-15 (as it was then called, per Larry) circulated with advisors and special-operations troops before general M16 issue — Larry's own weapon was a Thompson (VN-0013). The serious expression was posed. 'Heading back to headquarters' is Larry's stated assumption, not a memory.
